modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On July 7, 1952: The ocean liner SS United States passes Bishop Rock on her maiden voyage, breaking the transatlantic speed record to become the fastest passenger ship in the world.
On July 7, 1981: US President Ronald Reagan nominates Sandra Day O'Connor to become the first female member of the Supreme Court of the United States.
On July 7, 1937: The Peel Commission Report recommends the partition of Palestine, which was the first formal recommendation for partition in the history of Palestine.
On July 7, 1928: Sliced bread is sold for the first time (on the inventor's 48th birthday) by the Chillicothe Baking Company of Chillicothe, Missouri.
On July 7, 1907: Florenz Ziegfeld Jr. staged his first Follies on the roof of the New York Theater in New York City.
